metadata.title: Local Coding Agents on One Workstation, Second Night: What the Serving Stack, the Prompt and the Model Each Contribute
metadata.description:
The first night showed that open-weight models on one workstation could not yet replace a cloud worker on real application fixes, but its comparisons were run in blocks and its local servers were still defective. This second night repeats the question with paired arms: the two arms of a comparison start together on the same task, only one model server is loaded at a time, and the local runs are graded by the hidden tests of the fixes that actually landed.

Three findings stand out. First, naming the file and the function (the precise prompt) lifted the local Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B worker from 1 of 9 to 5 of 9 passes against the orchestrator's specification; all four discordant pairs favoured the precise prompt (exact sign test p = 0.125, two-sided). Second, serving still decided the outcome: a second model family ran through a multimodal code path that never hit the prefix cache, so every turn re-read 40-50k tokens; after the fix, a smoke run fell from 55-61 s to 23-37 s and a one-function fix ran within about twice the time of the cloud reference. Third, a cloud plan written from the parent commit let three different local models pass a task that none of eight local precise or specification runs passed.

A hardware watchdog reset, with about 117 GB of model servers resident on a 128 GB machine, set the constraint for the rest of the night: one model server at a time. The samples are small and every statement is conditional on them. The final ranking is Sonnet 5.5 (4 of 4) ahead of GLM-5.3-flash and GLM-5.3 (3 of 4 each), Haiku 4.5 (2 of 4) and then the local models; no local model passed the three-file task.

Second report of the PAI Reports series. Sources: https://github.com/mnott/PAI-Reports
